eyebrow: Four things that must fit in GPU memory
code:
# Training memory, not just the weights:
#
#   Parameters      - the weights themselves
#   Gradients       - one per parameter, from backward pass
#   Optimizer state - Adam's per-parameter moments (often FP32)
#   Activations     - intermediate outputs kept for backward pass
#
# Optimizer state is usually the BIGGEST of the four.
caption: A 7B model's raw FP16 weights are ~14GB, but training needs far more than that.

code:
# 7B-parameter model, mixed-precision Adam:
#
#   Parameters        ~14 GB   (FP16)
#   Gradients          ~14 GB   (FP16)
#   Optimizer state   ~56 GB   (2x FP32 moments)
#   -----------------------------------
#   Subtotal          ~84 GB   <- already past an 80GB GPU
#
# ...before a single activation is stored.
caption: The optimizer state, not the weights, is usually what breaks the memory budget first.
